# Helping your midwife find you
## A little planning for a warm welcome  
### Riverside Community Midwives

When you are having your baby at home, we want you to feel comfortable with the people coming through your door. In the Philippines, we say the midwife is like family. That is the feeling we hope to bring: a friendly face, someone you trust, and support when you need it.

But first, we need to find the right door.

Our team has plenty of experience caring for families. Finding a house with no number, behind an unmarked gate, at three in the morning? Sometimes that takes a little more help.

A few small things can make a big difference. You do not need a spotless house, matching towels or biscuits waiting on a plate. We just need to find you, park safely and get ourselves and our equipment inside.

## First things first: when to call

**Riverside home birth cover starts from 37 weeks of pregnancy.**

Before 37 weeks, if you think labour may be starting or your waters may have broken, contact your maternity team straight away. You will need assessment and care in hospital rather than a home birth. Follow the contact instructions in your maternity notes.

**From 37 weeks, phone the Riverside birth line when you think labour is starting.** You can also call if your waters break, or if you are unsure whether labour has started. You do not have to work it out on your own.

Use the birth line rather than your midwife’s personal mobile. The birth line reaches the midwife on call. Your usual midwife may be off duty, asleep or caring for another family.

**Riverside birth line: [insert number before sharing]**

When you call, please tell us:

- Your name and how many weeks pregnant you are.
- What is happening, including contractions and whether your waters have broken.
- Your full address and postcode, including any flat number.
- A phone number we can call you back on.
- Anything important about finding or entering your home.

**Please phone for labour advice. Do not rely on a text, WhatsApp message or location pin being seen.** If you cannot get through, use the alternative maternity contact number in your maternity notes.

Do not wait for labour to call about concerns such as reduced baby movements, bleeding or feeling unwell. Contact your maternity team promptly. In a life-threatening emergency, call **999**. If the baby appears to be coming now and no midwife is with you, call **999** and follow the call handler’s instructions.

## Give us the address — and the useful bits

Sat nav is helpful, but it has its moments. A house name alone can send us somewhere completely different. Lovely as a chippy may be, it is not where we need to be when your baby is arriving.

Please check that we have your full address, including:

- House number or name.
- Street name and postcode.
- Flat number, building name and floor, if needed.
- The entrance we should use.

Tell us about anything that could confuse a visitor. For example:

> “The entrance is on the side street, not the main road.”

> “Flat 14 is in the second building, through the blue gate.”

> “Our house has a name but no number. It is between numbers 22 and 26.”

If you live in a block of flats, please tell us about entry codes, intercoms, lifts and stairs. If the lift is broken or the intercom does not work, knowing beforehand really helps.

Share codes and personal location details privately with the team — not in the Facebook group.

## Make your door easy to spot

Please make sure your house number or name is visible from the street. A number hidden behind a hedge is playing hide-and-seek, and we would rather save our energy for looking after you.

At night, switch on your porch or outside light if you have one. A lit entrance makes a real difference on a dark winter street.

A bright ribbon or balloons on the gate can help too. One family did this and their home was wonderfully easy to find. It is completely optional: tell us what to look for, and keep anything you use clear of the path.

If someone is available, they could wave from the doorway or meet us at the entrance to the building. But please do not leave someone who needs support alone to go looking for us.

You do not need to leave your front door unlocked. Agree a safe way to let us in, and make sure someone can hear the doorbell or phone.

## A location pin can help

A map pin or what3words address can be useful, especially if your entrance is hard to find.

When you phone, ask the on-call midwife whether you can send it to the birth line phone on WhatsApp. Check that the pin marks the entrance we should use, rather than the middle of the building or the next street.

This is extra help, not a replacement for your full address or your phone call.

## Room for two cars, if possible

**Two midwives attend the birth, usually travelling in separate cars.** If possible, please help us find two nearby parking spaces.

We bring quite a lot with us: gas and air cylinders, a large equipment bag and sometimes equipment for a birth pool. Our arms appreciate a short journey from the car.

If you cannot arrange parking, please do not worry. Tell us where we can legally park and whether there is a long walk, a narrow passage or steps.

If you live in a permit area, including parts of Anfield and Kensington, check the rules for your street in advance. Ask the council about visitor permits if needed. Have any valid permits ready and let us know how to use them. Depending on the scheme, they may need activating or displaying in our vehicles.

Please do not assume that being a midwife means we can park anywhere. Sadly, a big bag and a purposeful walk do not count as a parking permit.

## A clear path, not a perfect house

There is no need for a big clean before we arrive. This is a birth visit, not a house inspection.

Please clear a safe route from the entrance to the room you plan to use. Move shoes, bags, washing baskets and loose toys out of the way. Keep any stairs we need to use clear too.

Lego is wonderful. Lego under a foot carrying equipment is less wonderful.

Let us know about slippery steps, uneven paths or anything else we should watch out for.

## Give pets their own quiet space

We know pets are part of the family. Many of us love them too.

Even a friendly dog can get excited when new people arrive with interesting bags. Please arrange for pets to stay safely in another room or with someone who can care for them, away from the entrance and birth space.

We would love a calm welcome. We are less steady with a cylinder in our arms and an enthusiastic dog around our knees.

---

## Fridge checklist: ready to welcome your midwives

### Before 37 weeks
☐ Save the **Riverside birth line: [insert number]**.  
☐ Keep your maternity notes and alternative contact number handy.  
☐ Check we have your full address, postcode and entrance details.  
☐ Tell us about entry codes, stairs, lifts or access difficulties.  
☐ Check parking rules and arrange visitor permits if needed.  
☐ Plan a safe, quiet place for pets.

### When labour starts
☐ **Phone the birth line — not a midwife’s personal mobile.**  
☐ Confirm your address and callback number.  
☐ Explain where to park and how to get inside.  
☐ Send a location pin only as agreed with the midwife.

### Before we arrive, if possible
☐ Switch on the outside light at night.  
☐ Make sure your house number or name is easy to see.  
☐ Have parking permits ready, if needed.  
☐ Clear the path, hallway and any stairs we will use.  
☐ Settle pets safely away from the entrance and birth space.  
☐ Keep your phone nearby so we can reach you.

**If things happen quickly, do not worry about finishing the list. Call for help first. You and your baby matter more than parking spaces, porch lights or washing baskets.**

We look forward to meeting your baby — and finding your front door on the first try.

**With love,  
Riverside Community Midwives**
